Details: The test `testGenerateURLFragment` checks whether HTML entities such as `"` are correctly escaped to their corresponding character by the `StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment` method. However, the test failure indicates that this is not the case. Consequently, un-escaped strings are being returned, which leads to the error demonstrated by the test.

The test `['org.apache.commons.cli.PatternOptionBuilderTest.testExistingFilePatternFileNotExist()']` failed.
The test looks like:

```java
174 :     @Test
175 :     public void testExistingFilePatternFileNotExist() throws Exception {
176 :         final Options options = PatternOptionBuilder.parsePattern("f<");
177 :         final CommandLineParser parser = new PosixParser();
178 :         final CommandLine line = parser.parse(options, new String[] { "-f", "non-existing.file" });
179 : 
180 :         assertNull("option f parsed", line.getOptionObject("f")); // error occurred here
181 :     }
```

It failed with the following error message and call stack:

```
junit.framework.AssertionFailedError: option f parsed expected null, but was:<non-existing.file>
	at org.junit.Assert.fail(Assert.java:88)
	at org.junit.Assert.failNotNull(Assert.java:664)
	at org.junit.Assert.assertNull(Assert.java:646)
	at org.apache.commons.cli.PatternOptionBuilderTest.testExistingFilePatternFileNotExist(PatternOptionBuilderTest.java:180)
```

The failing test `testExistingFilePatternFileNotExist` is related to the `PatternOptionBuilder.parsePattern(java.lang.String)` method because the test calls this method to get an `Options` object which is then parsed by the `PosixParser`. The test expects that the option "f" with an existing file pattern will not parse a non-existing filename and returns `null` when calling `line.getOptionObject("f")`. However, it actually returns the string "non-existing.file".
